result:
The proposed answer 1012 is wrong. The claimed extremal configuration is not extremal.

**Coefficients.** Write P − Q = Σ c_i a_i with a_1 ≤ … ≤ a_n. For an element of rank i, let q = n − i be the number of larger elements. Element i is the median of an odd subset when it has equally many smaller and larger partners, contributing +1. It is one of the two middle elements of an even subset when the numbers of smaller and larger partners differ by exactly 1, contributing +1/2 each time. With N = n − 1 = 2024, this gives

c_i = f(q) = C(N,q) − ½[C(N,q−1) + C(N,q+1)].

I checked this directly on n = 3 (giving P − Q = a_2) and n = 5 (c_3 = 2, c_5 = −1).

**Extreme points.** Since the a_i are sorted with max = 1, the maximum of Σ c_i a_i is attained at a = (0,…,0,1,…,1). So C is the maximum of the suffix sums S(m) = Σ_{q=0}^{m} f(q) over 0 ≤ m ≤ N. Telescoping gives

S(m) = ½ + ½[C(N,m) − C(N,m+1)].

**Counterexample.** Take m = 2022, i.e. a_1 = a_2 → 0⁺ and a_3 = … = a_2025 = 1. Then

P − Q → ½ + ½[C(2024,2022) − C(2024,2023)] = ½ + ½(2047276 − 2024) = 1022626.5.

This exceeds 1012, so C ≥ 1022626.5 and the answer 1012 cannot be correct.

**Small-case check.** For n = 7 the same method gives suffix sums −2, −4, −2, 3, 5, 3, 1, so C = 5, not (n−1)/2 = 3. The proposed claim that the configuration with one tiny element is extremal fails already at n = 7, and the argument for it was never justified.

The true C is much larger than 1012. It equals max over m of ½ + ½[C(2024,m) − C(2024,m+1)], which is on the order of 2^2024 divided by a polynomial in 2024.

VERDICT: REJECT
